title: How qteasy's parts fit together
summary: Local data, a data panel, strategies run by an Operator, then backtest, optimization, and simulated live trading.
narrative:
qteasy is one pipeline.

Local data store (DataSource). Downloads from Tushare or other channels land in local tables. Which channel or table to use is a separate question.

HistoryPanel. This is the in-memory panel for looking at and analyzing that data.

Strategies and Operator. Built-in or custom strategies declare the data they need. An Operator runs them.

Backtest. It evaluates a strategy on historical data and reports the result.

Optimization. It searches parameters of a strategy.

Simulated live. The same strategy logic runs on a live-style schedule. Ask can explain the boundary. It does not start a trader or send orders.

This card only names the parts. Ask a self-contained question for any one of them, for example how to backtest with qteasy.
risk_notes: Naming a module does not download data, run a backtest, or start simulated live trading.
